metaData.originalTitle: 不用手搓 SQL 验数了！阿里生产级端到端 Agent Skill 完整设计复盘
metaData.title: No More Manual SQL for Data Validation! Complete Design Review of Alibaba's Production-Grade End-to-End Agent Skill
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a detailed review of the design of Alibaba's production-grade data validation Agent Skill (verify-data), covering the full workflow from natural language trigger to automatically generating validation SQL, executing it, and producing reports, including architecture, core capabilities, real-world cases, design principles, and lessons learned.
metaData.summary: This article, aimed at data development teams, systematically introduces an end-to-end data validation Agent Skill called verify-data. Starting from the pain points of manual validation (insufficient coverage, wrong base table selection, code understanding偏差, conclusions without evidence, high overhead of consolidation), it explains the opportunity for Agent-driven validation. The core part breaks down the 7-9 step workflow of verify-data (which can actually reach 17 conditionally triggered steps), including automatic base table discovery (lineage + two-stage ranking of dimensions and metrics), 10 types of standardized validation SQL templates, Code Diff-driven scanning of 8 types of risk signals, 4 fallback validation strategies, partition pre-check and batched execution strategy, and three critical mandatory steps (base table suitability pre-check, dimension table CUBE detection, and logical mapping check). The effectiveness is demonstrated through four real-world scenarios: onboarding a new CUBE table, DEV vs PROD comparison, a brand-new metric without a base table, and dimension table validation. The article extracts four hard red lines (no skipping templates to write custom SQL, no guessing field mappings, fallback must incorporate code review, must verify all JOIN explosions and date associations), and provides a PASS/WARNING/FAIL conclusion system. Lessons learned include that NULLs in CUBE summary rows are normal behavior, tolerance for floating-point precision, and that DWD recomputation is structurally homogeneous and can only prove execution consistency. Current challenges include execution latency, permission dependencies, trust cost of fallback, and onboarding difficulty. Finally, it outlines three future directions: asynchronous execution, platform integration, and intelligent root cause localization.

mainPoints.point: Base table auto-discovery is the core capability of verify-data, using a two-stage strategy of lineage-based candidate collection and metric/dimension ranking to automatically select the best comparison benchmark.
mainPoints.explanation: When the user does not provide a base table, the Agent traces upstream tables via lineage and calculates a composite score based on lineage affinity, dimension overlap, and metric overlap. A score ≥ 0.7 leads to direct selection; if multiple tables can jointly cover metrics, they are compared in separate branches; if no suitable base table is found, fallback strategies are triggered.

mainPoints.point: 10 types of standardized validation SQL templates ensure verification coverage; especially association explosion detection and date association validation are the most common reasons for review rejection.
mainPoints.explanation: The templates include total comparison, data quality check, dimension-by-dimension comparison, dimension table partition validation, CUBE integrity check, summary row consistency, logical relationship validation, historical trend comparison, association explosion detection, and date association validation. Four of them are mandatory.

mainPoints.point: Code Diff-driven risk scanning pinpoints the impact of specific code changes on data, bridging the gap from 'knowing how much is different' to 'knowing why it's different'.
mainPoints.explanation: In iterative validation scenarios, the Agent retrieves DEV and PROD running code, performs a structured diff, scans for 8 types of risk signals (data source changes, JOIN relationship changes, aggregation method changes, etc.), and generates quantified confirmation SQL for each high-risk signal.

mainPoints.point: Fallback validation strategies ensure meaningful conclusions even without a base table, but they mandate additional code review and independent construction of V-type confirmation SQL to prevent self-confirming execution consistency.
mainPoints.explanation: Four fallback strategies (CUBE self-consistency, DWD recomputation, separate branch metrics, static logic) are automatically selected based on table type. During fallback, in addition to running D-type consistency SQL, 8 types of risk scanning must be performed and V-type quantified confirmation SQL must be generated independently of the original logic.

keyQuotes: Upgrade traditional manual validation from 'writing multiple SQL queries + manual comparison' to 'one-sentence trigger + review-grade evidence output'.
Standardization is more important than intelligence: the key to validation is coverage and repeatability; 10 types of standardized templates are far more reliable than 'letting AI improvise'.
Lessons-learned records are core assets: the 19 real-world experiences documented in lessons-learned.md, each one is a real pitfall we stepped into.
Red lines must be hard: critical red lines are enforced at the process level, not 'suggestions' but 'mandatory'.

relatedArticles.title: Rethinking the AI Revolution: Has Software Engineering Ever Truly Been "Engineered" in the Past 50 Years?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: From an engineering philosophy perspective, this article argues that software engineering has not truly been engineered in the past five decades. It posits that large language models (LLMs) have, for the first time, achieved "exchanging energy for high-level intelligence," marking the true arrival of software engineering. It systematically deduces a new AI-centric paradigm, implementation pathways, and the evolution of human roles.
